title: xgboost
description: Performs label transfer from reference to query using XGBoost classifier

dataset input.title: Dataset input
dataset input.description: Dataset input using nf-tower "dataset" or "data explorer". Allows for the input of multiple parameter sets to initialise a Nextflow channel.

param_list.description: Dataset input can either be a list of maps, a csv file, a json file, a yaml file, or simply a yaml blob. The names of the input fields (e.g. csv columns, json keys) need to be an exact match with the workflow input parameters.

input.description: The query data to transfer the labels to. Should be a .h5mu file.
input.help_text: type: `string`, multiple: False, required, direction: `input`, example: `['input.h5mu']`

input_obsm_features.description:
The `.obsm` key of the embedding to use for the classifier's inference. If not provided, the `.X` slot will be used instead.
Make sure that embedding was obtained in the same way as the reference embedding (e.g. by the same model or preprocessing).

reference.description: The reference data to train classifiers on.

reference_obsm_features.description:
The `.obsm` key of the embedding to use for the classifier's training. If not provided, the `.X` slot will be used instead.
Make sure that embedding was obtained in the same way as the query embedding (e.g. by the same model or preprocessing).

reference_obs_targets.description: The `.obs` key(s) of the target labels to transfer.

output.description: The query data in .h5mu format with predicted labels transferred from the reference.

output_obs_predictions.description:
In which `.obs` slots to store the predicted information.
If provided, must have the same length as `--reference_obs_targets`.
If empty, will default to the `reference_obs_targets` combined with the `"_pred"` suffix.

output_obs_probability.description:
In which `.obs` slots to store the probability of the predictions.
If provided, must have the same length as `--reference_obs_targets`.
If empty, will default to the `reference_obs_targets` combined with the `"_probability"` suffix.

output_compression.description:
Compression format to use for the output AnnData and/or Mudata H5 files.
By default no compression is applied.

force_retrain.description: Retrain models on the reference even if model_output directory already has trained classifiers. WARNING! It will rewrite existing classifiers for targets in the model_output directory!

use_gpu.description: Use GPU during models training and inference (recommended).

verbosity.description: The verbosity level for evaluation of the classifier from the range [0,2]

model_output.help_text: type: `string`, multiple: False, default: `model`, direction: `output`, example: `['path/to/model']`

output_uns_parameters.description: The key in `uns` slot of the output AnnData object to store the parameters of the XGBoost classifier.

learning_rate.description: Step size shrinkage used in update to prevents overfitting. Range: [0,1]. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

min_split_loss.description: Minimum loss reduction required to make a further partition on a leaf node of the tree. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

max_depth.description: Maximum depth of a tree. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

min_child_weight.description: Minimum sum of instance weight (hessian) needed in a child. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

max_delta_step.description: Maximum delta step we allow each leaf output to be. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

subsample.description: Subsample ratio of the training instances. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

sampling_method.description: The method to use to sample the training instances. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

colsample_bytree.description: Fraction of columns to be subsampled. Range (0, 1]. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

colsample_bylevel.description: Subsample ratio of columns for each level. Range (0, 1]. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

colsample_bynode.description: Subsample ratio of columns for each node (split). Range (0, 1]. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

reg_lambda.description: L2 regularization term on weights. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

reg_alpha.description: L1 regularization term on weights. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

scale_pos_weight.description: Control the balance of positive and negative weights, useful for unbalanced classes. See https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html#parameters-for-tree-booster for the reference

nextflow input-output arguments.title: Nextflow input-output arguments
nextflow input-output arguments.description: Input/output parameters for Nextflow itself. Please note that both publishDir and publish_dir are supported but at least one has to be configured.
